findings.title: rejectedEmails array is shared across all controller instances
findings.body: Declaring `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` directly on the class body puts a single array on the prototype, shared by every instance of CreateAccountController (and never reset when the modal is reopened). Because the code mutates it with `pushObject`, emails rejected in one session stay rejected forever for the page lifetime, and any other instance sees them too. Initialize it per-instance (e.g. in `init`, `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))`) and clear it when the modal is shown.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive and not normalized
findings.body: `should_block?` does an exact `where(email: email)` match. Emails in the users table are stored/compared downcased elsewhere (see `Email.downcase` usage), but blocked entries are stored verbatim from the migration/fabricator with no normalization callback. A blocked address such as `bad@spam.com` is trivially bypassed by signing up as `Bad@Spam.com`. Downcase/strip the email both before persisting a BlockedEmail and in the lookup.

findings.title: match_count update uses non-atomic save and ignores failures
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads-modifies-writes outside a transaction, so concurrent signups with the same blocked email lose counts, and a failed `save` (e.g. validation) is silently swallowed while the block decision still proceeds. Prefer an atomic `update_all`/`increment!`-style SQL update.

findings.title: Signup failure response now echoes full error hash and submitted values
findings.body: The create response now includes `user.errors.to_hash` and the submitted name/username/email. This makes account enumeration easier programmatically (e.g. distinguishing "email already taken" from other failures) and reflects user input back into JSON. If only the email rejection flag is needed by the client, return a minimal, specific field instead of the whole error hash.

findings.title: No specs cover whitelist/blacklist behaviour after move out of User
findings.body: The domain whitelist/blacklist logic was removed from `User#email_validator` and moved here, but the new spec only stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?`. If the existing user specs referenced the removed private methods they would break, and either way the whitelist/blacklist branches of the new validator are untested, so a regression in the regex construction would go unnoticed.
